notes_for_editor: First-lighting date is genuinely disputed (see resolved_conflicts); the story lists the claims rather than choosing. Heap says the site is 3.5 miles from the Delaware shore while the NRHP and Lighthousefriends say some 12 miles east of Bowers; the story gives only the NRHP figure. Record 'conflicts' (structure positions more than 500 m apart) not investigated or resolved. Lighthousefriends facts (Buelton rescue, 1917-18 ice, lens loan, 2005 excess and 2007 auction, final Coast Guard crew 1973, H. A. Ramsay & Son) rest on that one secondary source; the 1937 Bulletin and Lighthousefriends differ with other sources on small points (Lighthousefriends gives two weeks for Robinson's broken ankle, the Democratic Messenger six). The Democratic Messenger names the keeper Lewis E. Robinson; USLHS has Lewis F. The Milford Chronicle (1923) says 'Leroy Smith' succeeded Mitchell; USLHS has Lee R. Smith (not used in the story). Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1937 pages 18 and 38 are two-column OCR with interleaved lines; the quotes are contiguous fragments within one line, so the checker should confirm against the page image. Light-House Board report volumes were matched to fiscal years by their title pages (1892, 1894, 1896, 1899, 1900); fog-signal hours are OCR readings and printed page numbers were not confirmed (cited by volume/scan page). Fog-signal note: Heap and the Board reports say Daboll trumpet with hot-air engines; the 1937 Bulletin calls the original signal a reed horn, the district's first compressed-air signal (not used in the story). The USCG Historian's page for this light (reported by search as saying automated 1972) could not be read (403/404 through the archive), so DBLHKFA is cited for 1972. Spicer's other-station entries rest on the Bulletin obituary; the Marcus Hook entry carries no id because the Bulletin's 'Marcus Hook Range Rear' was not matched to a map station. The roster (129 lines) is copied from the USLHS place page, with 'person' slugs from roster.py; Coast Guard personnel after 1959 are listed as the archive prints them. Moro Castle anecdote also appears in the NRHP nomination quoting Snow (1955). No Wikipedia text was used. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the nomination's 'twelve miles east of Bowers' conflicts with Heap and the Cape Gazette (about 3.5 miles); the story now states the disagreement. The 1917 efficiency-flag table (Chester P. Joseph for the fourth district) was matched by column position in OCR and the keeper column's 'jr.' belongs to Wakefield of the third district. 'Listed 1989' rests on the NRIS number 89000286 and the NPGallery date published 3/27/1989; the nomination's own Keeper date is not legible in the OCR. Robinson is called Keeper in the Democratic Messenger, assistant by Lighthouse Friends and the USLHS archive.
